racking_stepping_supplement.notes: No Illusions/Eastern Wholesale Fence-branded slope-installation guide, racking chart, or max rake angle in degrees or rise-per-foot was located for V3707/Grand Illusions or any Illusions series. Illusions' own Installation Instructions PDF and GATES Instructions PDF (already in manuals/) do not mention racking, stepping, or slope installation at all -- this remains a confirmed gap in Illusions' published literature, not merely an unindexed document. General industry data (non-Illusions, for context only, NOT to be attributed to Illusions): competitor/industry guides cite natural racking limits of roughly 10 degrees before requiring enlarged routed holes, with absolute limits around 15-35 degrees depending on style (privacy panels rack the least, ~3in over an 8ft section per Hoover Fence; picket/post-rail styles rack more). These numbers are explicitly NOT Illusions-sourced and should not be used as authoritative for Illusions products.

post_spacing_supplement.source: Miami-Dade NOA 14-1209.01 PE-stamped structural drawings (Dixon Engineering, Inc.)
post_spacing_supplement.caveat: The install manuals still say only 'see appropriate style spec sheet' for on-center spacing (confirmed again this pass -- Illusions-Vinyl-Fence-Installation-Instructions_0224.pdf and the assembled-panel instructions both defer to a per-style spec sheet rather than stating spacing directly). The NOA structural drawings DO show dimensioned panel/foundation layouts per style, reproduced below as documented -- but the overall dimension callouts on the shop drawings describe the drawn foundation-to-foundation footprint for the pictured 2-post test section, not an explicit 'post spacing O.C. = X inches' label. We report the as-drawn numbers without inferring an O.C. spacing value that isn't explicitly labeled, per the instruction not to fabricate.

aluminum_post_insert_api9.additional_detail_found: API9 = 4.5in x 4.5in x 9ft aluminum post insert, sized to run the full length of a 9ft post (matches standard post length for up to 6-8ft fence height), so it is a full-length insert rather than a partial-depth insert -- no separate 'insertion depth' spec exists because it is not a partial fill. Confirmed in Illusions Vinyl Fence Spring Product Catalog (2019) accessories section and Illusions' Aluminum Post Inserts product page.
aluminum_post_insert_api9.bom_confirmation: The NOA-certified structural drawings list a generic 'POST INSERT' line item (qty 2 per post) in the bill of materials for the 75MPH-rated sections, consistent with a post insert being part of the certified/tested assembly, though the drawings do not name it as API9 specifically.

steel_post_reinforcement.notes: No Illusions/Eastern Wholesale Fence-branded steel post insert or steel reinforcement product was found. Illusions' own marketing (buyvinylfence.com dealer page, profencesupply.com) explicitly states Illusions posts 'do not need inserts' due to 100% virgin vinyl construction, and contrasts this with competitor products that require wood inserts. Steel inserts, rebar, and post stiffeners referenced in this pass (ISP Fence, Alliance Fence & Supply, Hoover Fence, mftfence.com) are generic third-party/aftermarket products for vinyl fence in general, NOT Illusions-branded or Illusions-specified components. This is a confirmed gap: Illusions does not appear to publish its own steel reinforcement or rebar spec.

gate_and_corner_post_practice.illusions_specific: Illusions Heavy Duty posts (VH55, VH88 series, 0.250in average wall thickness) are specified by Illusions for gate posts and high-wind/corner applications, per the general Installation Instructions and Gate Installation Instructions PDFs (already in manuals/). No Illusions-published rebar sizing or rebar-in-post spec was found.
gate_and_corner_post_practice.generic_industry_practice_not_illusions_: Hoover Fence generic guidance: end/gate posts filled with concrete plus 2 pieces of 1/2in rebar, rebar run from bottom of hole to half the post height (end posts) or 12in down from top (gate posts), using rebar separator clips to hold rebar in opposing corners. This is explicitly a third-party (Hoover Fence) practice, not confirmed as an Illusions-specified method.
